name: Tanglang-Toloza
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Tanglang-Toloza (Loloish): only comparative/subgrouping refs (Lama 2012 diss., Bradley 2002); no descriptive phonology of Tanglang located

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login
sources.note: Toloza profile p.80 (the text layer): 'Toloza [tho55lo33zɑ33] is spoken in Tai'an of Lijiang County.. 35 initials, 48 vowels.., 3 tones (/55/, /33/, and /21/) (cf. YYFC 1983)'; Table 4.18 (p.106) lists Toloza tonemes 55 33 53 32 21. The words 'stress' and 'accent' occur nowhere in the dissertation (a full-text search for stress/accent count 0).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record tang1372 and reference records 475782 (Gai & Wang 2013) and 548889 (Gai 2002); Wikipedia 'Tholo language' / 堂郎語.
sources.note: Bibliographic/encyclopedic only: Glottolog lists exactly two descriptive works (the 2002 sketch and 2013 phonology); Wikipedia gives location, autonym tʰo42 lo42 (zɑ33) and cites Gai 2002 and Bradley 2004; no phonology section.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene S. L. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages: Tanglang (data from Prof. Gai Xingzhi, Yunnan Nationality University, 24 Oct 2009).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Numerals 1-10,000 with tone digits (53, 33, 55, 42, 44, 31) and a note that Tanglang is 'a newly discovered seriously endangered language.. about two thousand people'; no stress statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-110 (D. Bradley): create [ytl] Tanglang; adopted 2008-01-14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Administrative request citing Bradley 2004 and Gai 2002 as sources; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Bradley, David. 2004. Endangered Central Ngwi Languages of Northwestern Yunnan. Keynote, 37th International Conference on Sino-Tibetan Languages and Linguistics, Lund University, October 2004. 13 pp. (academia.edu 5737342)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic note only: 'Tanglang: SW Lijiang County, southern Tai'an Township. 947 people in eight villages; also a few in adjacent areas of Jianchuan County. Most including children can speak the language.. long-term Bai cultural influence, also in contact with Naxi. Potentially endangered. See Yunnan (1983) and Gai (2002).' Table 2 gives Tanglang 'dog/fire/tile' with tone digits; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.note: The primary grammar sketch (Glottolog's only sketch); Minzu Yuwen 概况 articles have a fixed 语音 section (声母/韵母/声调, sometimes 重音) followed by grammar; cited by Bradley 2004, ISO CR 2007-110 and Lama 2012 as the source on Tanglang.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Tanglang ('first comprehensive phonological analysis'); a Chinese 语音 article of this type normally has a 声调 section and often a line on 重音/轻声; keywords include tone sandhi.
